verifiedRecords.probability: For every fixed v, expectation is over the random tape. Choosing the theorem’s failure parameter as n^{−c} and taking a union bound gives poly(Δ)·log n cost simultaneously for all vertices with high probability.
verifiedRecords.state: One fixed random tape defines the same global MIS in the reduction graph and hence one consistent coloring across all requests
verifiedRecords.adaptivity: The fixed-v expectation does not automatically hold for a vertex selected after observing the random tape or earlier answers. The simultaneous high-probability event is a separate guarantee.
reduction: Retain exactly degree(v)+1 colors from each list, in a fixed order.
Use a vertex (v,c) for each retained color. Join all copies of v into a clique and connect (u,c) to (v,c) when uv is an original edge and c occurs in both lists.
The reduction graph has N≤n(Δ+1) vertices and maximum degree at most 2Δ. Maximality forces exactly one selected copy of each v, since at most degree(v) colors can be blocked by neighbors.

An original color query can check at most Δ+1 fixed MIS vertices. Simulating each reduction-graph neighborhood uses only polynomially many original graph/list probes. Thus the unspecified polynomial remains polynomial and log N=O(log n).
assumptions: Readable vertex lists of size at least degree(v)+1, fixed graph ordering and fixed shared randomness
Expectation applies to each fixed queried vertex, not the expected maximum over queries
The high-probability and expected guarantees describe the same reduction-based algorithm
Polynomial reduction overhead is absorbed into poly(Δ); no exact polynomial exponent is supplied

relatedResults.bound: Theorem 10 reports O(k^9 log k) average-case probes and O(k^26 polylog k) average-case time
relatedResults.guarantee: Consistent proper exact k-coloring with high probability over graph/coins
relatedResults.sourceLocation: Theorem 10, Appendix A.2; Definitions A.2–A.4 (arXiv v1 printed pp.37–40)
relatedResults.notes: Preserved as a related result with a visible source-audit qualification. The source theorem is verified in both HTML and PDF, but its O(k^9 log k) count is not placed on the main adjacency-list cost axis or advertised as an exact adjacency-matrix pair-probe bound.
relatedResults.quality: Exact k-coloring under the uniform distribution over k-colorable labeled graphs; zero-error partial answers or FAIL
relatedResults.displayBound: Reported O(k^9 log k) probes; probe unit unresolved
relatedResults.graph: Uniformly sampled labeled k-colorable n-vertex graph, for 2≤k≤n^{1/37}; not worst-case graph input
relatedResults.output: Consistent proper partial k-coloring with FAIL on remaining vertices; full proper k-coloring on the high-probability graph event
relatedResults.parameters: n, k and a fixed shared random tape; no persistent memory between output queries
relatedResults.oracle: Appendix A uses a generic graph-probe convention. The main full-output algorithm is adjacency-matrix based, but the exact local O(k^9 log k) theorem must not be labeled a verified pair-query bound.
relatedResults.probability: Zero-error: never return an improper partial coloring. Definitions A.3–A.4 require full coloring with probability at least 1−1/n over the graph distribution; the proof gives a 1−exp(−Ω(n/k)) graph-structure event. Shared random choices are kept consistent.
relatedResults.state: Every query erases local memory; all queries use the same random tape to select and deterministically color the same core
relatedResults.adaptivity: The probe quantity is E_G[max_v E_r Q(G,v)], not E_{G,v,r} Q and not E_G E_r[max_v Q]
relatedResults.theorem: Theorem 10; Definitions A.1–A.4; Algorithm 14 and proof, Appendix A; Definition 4.2
relatedResults.timeBound: O(k^26 polylog k) average-case time, averaged over graphs and queried vertices as defined in Appendix A
relatedResults.queryQuantifier: E_G[max_v E_r Q(G,v)] = O(k^9 log k), using the paper’s reported probe convention
assumptions: Uniform distribution over all labeled k-colorable graphs, not G(n,p) and not arbitrary worst-case graphs
A fixed shared random tape; zero-error allows FAIL

The local probe unit is unresolved: the proof charges O(ν) probes for a sampled core with ν=Θ(k^9 log k) vertices, while certifying its induced adjacency matrix would ordinarily need pair-entry accounting
The full-output Ω(nk) lower bound is not a lower bound for these local queries
